text:
Predicates:
ScheduleMeeting(x, y) ::: Employee x schedules a meeting with customer y.
Appear(x, y) ::: Employee x appears in the company on day y.
LunchInCompany(x) ::: Person x has lunch in the company.
LunchAtHome(x) ::: Person x has lunch at home.
RemoteWork(x) ::: Person x works remotely from home.
InOtherCountries(x) ::: Person x is in other countries.
Manager(x) ::: Person x is a manager.
Premises:
∀x ∀y (ScheduleMeeting(x, y) → Appear(x, today)) ::: All employees who schedule a meeting with their customers will appear in the company today.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) → ∃y ScheduleMeeting(x, y)) ::: Everyone who has lunch in the company schedules meetings with their customers.
∀x (LunchInCompany(x) ∨ LunchAtHome(x)) ::: Employees will either have lunch in the company or have lunch at home.
∀x (LunchAtHome(x) → RemoteWork(x)) ::: If an employee has lunch at home, then he/she is working remotely from home.
∀x (InOtherCountries(x) → RemoteWork(x)) ::: All employees who are in other countries work remotely from home.
∀x (Manager(x) → ¬RemoteWork(x)) ::: No managers work remotely from home.
(Manager(james) ∧ Appear(james, today)) ⊕ ¬(Manager(james) ∨ Appear(james, today)) ::: James is either a manager and appears in the company today or neither a manager nor appears in the company today.
Conclusion:
LunchInCompany(james) ::: James has lunch in the company.
